articles.title: Country diary: A new chapter for the farm – we’re going organic | Andrea Meanwell
articles.description: Tebay, Cumbria: Historically it’s been a tricky thing for hill farms to do, but we’ve always run ours on organic principles, and now we’re fully converting From 1 November we have change happening on our farm. We have decided to become an organic farm and have started the two-year conversion process with the Soil Association. We’ve always run the farm on organic principles, but now, with our small shop selling our beef, lamb and pork, we’ve decided that we will convert, prioritising soil health and biodiversity without the use of chemicals. It has historically been tricky for hill farms to go organic because many are on commons with shared grazing and no physical boundaries between “hefts”, and with shared routes to and from the fell. Now the certifiers are keen to be flexible and adapt, so we have decided to give it a go. The process is funded by the government’s sustainable farming incentive scheme, which we were lucky to get into this year as so many farmers missed out. Continue reading...

articles.title: California weather is ‘well into extreme territory’ with historic high tides
articles.description: Seawater surges into low-lying communities from San Diego to San Francisco Bay Area, submerging streets, homes and businesses Historic high tides have caused chaos up and down the California coast this week, as parts of the state were inundated by record-breaking water levels. Seawater surged into low-lying communities from San Diego to the San Francisco Bay Area, submerging streets, flooding homes and businesses, and jamming important transportation corridors and train routes. Kayakers and paddle boarders could be seen gliding through typically busy thoroughfares in Marin county, north of San Francisco, on Monday and Tuesday. Several drivers had to be rescued from floating cars in the area, while cyclists who had attempted to cross the temporary lagoon that had formed quickly found themselves waist-deep. Further south, in cities such as Newport Beach, water pounded the emergency infrastructure set up to keep out the swelling sea, which seeped through berms, seawalls and sandbag blockades along the shoreline. articles.title: Brazil Investigates Possible Election Interference From JD Vance Group
articles.description: A Brazilian judge has ordered an investigation into a donor network co-founded by Vice President JD Vance, saying it may have aided right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil’s presidential election. The Washington Post reports that Brazil Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino has ordered Brazilian federal police to investigate the contacts between Vance’s Rockbridge Network and any Brazilian political operatives or companies. It’s illegal in Brazil for political candidates to accept assistance or aid from overseas. Dino wrote the investigation was “necessary to verify if there was the effective furnishment of resources—including human resources—services, or other measurable economic advantages, identifying its origin, its destination and its eventual use in the campaign.” Vance has spoken at Rockbridge events within the last year. The donor organization denied any contacts with Brazilian officials, and Vance’s office declined to comment to the Post. Rockbridge received multiple complaints during Brazil’s elections. The Workers’ Party led by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who defeated Bolsonaro, filed one with the country’s Supreme Court, while Renan Santos, a right-wing presidential candidate who was eliminated in the first round of voting, went to the country’s Supreme Electoral Court. Santos said that Brazilians who claimed to represent Rockbridge had spoken with Bolsonaro campaign officials about providing support. An unnamed source said they also reached out to Santos offering campaign help. Rockbridge denied any connections with the Brazilians claiming to represent it. “The Brazilians made false representations about their relationship with Rockbridge and created documents representing or referencing Rockbridge without Rockbridge’s knowledge or consent,” the network said in a statement Tuesday. Bolsonaro is under investigation for fraud and money laundering in Brazil, and has fled to the U.S. after the State Department reportedly granted him and his family visas. He left before Brazilian police could seize his passport, as the country’s Supreme Court had ordered. If Vance’s group was helping Bolsonaro, that would only add to his charges, and show how far the Trump administration is willing to interfere in other countries’ elections even as it fearmongers about the same happening in the U.S.

articles.title: Another Cowardly Bolsonaro Comes Crying to Donald Trump
articles.description: This week, a would-be far-right presidential dynasty in South America’s largest country died before our very eyes. On Monday, the day after losing Brazil’s presidential election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro went to visit his father. Former President Jair Bolsonaro is under house arrest, serving a 27-year sentence for plotting to overturn his defeat in the 2022 election. Immediately upon leaving, Flávio, who has been implicated in a money-laundering scheme, was reportedly approached by Federal Police agents who demanded he hand over his passport; the man who a week ago was widely expected to become Brazil’s next president was being told not to leave the country. In a video filmed shortly thereafter, Flávio criticized the authorities for their gung-ho attitude. “I never considered leaving the country,” he said, insisting, “I’m going to deliver my passports and defend myself from this aberration, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me. But nobody is going to silence me.” Less than a day later, the younger Bolsonaro was gone. On Wednesday morning, he landed in Miami, after President Trump’s State Department stated that it would issue visas to the senator and his family. His arrival in the United States early Wednesday morning represents a new chapter in the Bolsonaro family’s expanding efforts to coordinate the Brazilian opposition from under Trump’s skirt. Flávio’s brother, former Congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro, self-exiled to Texas a year ago so that he could lobby MAGA-world full-time on father’s behalf, for which Brazil’s Supreme Court sentenced him in absentia to more than four years in prison. Though they may have to remind the senescent U.S. president who they are from time to time, Flávio and Eduardo have successfully evaded Brazilian justice. The Donroe Doctrine, Trump’s strategy for Western hemispheric dominance, apparently includes selectively overriding other nations’ sovereign authority to prosecute criminal offenses when the accused are his political supplicants. But not even the authoritarian leader of the world’s most powerful country can save the ignominious Bolsonaros from political irrelevance. Flávio may be safe for now from any accountability for his misdeeds in his home country. But he has effectively surrendered any claim to Brazilian political leadership for himself or another member of his clan. Indeed, as I wrote in August, one of the questions facing the Brazilian far right early in this campaign was whether one of the disgraced former president’s sons was really the best candidate to run against an incumbent with middling poll numbers in Lula. Why not put up, say, a popular governor who had served in the elder Bolsonaro’s Cabinet but did not carry the blighted last name of the far-right leader? Jair Bolsonaro’s insistence on running Flávio, against the advice of many in his ideological camp, strained his coalition—even more so since Flávio lost. For Flávio now to flee, apparently without warning even close allies, is to concede that the family is not up to the task of sustaining the opposition. Flávio’s own campaign manager admitted he had no idea where the senator was: “We are surprised because yesterday we spoke about the necessity of Flávio, with the 60 million votes he received, assuming this role of opposition leader.” That is the role Flávio had proclaimed for himself even as he was apparently planning his getaway. For Flávio to leave so abruptly is also to surrender his father to his fate. Trump already applied considerable pressure on Brazil on Jair’s behalf, to no effect. The former president’s wife just won a Senate seat, as did another one of his sons; another won a seat in the lower house of Congress. But the only plausible hope for Jair Bolsonaro to leave jail anytime soon was probably for Flávio to win the presidency, empowering Flávio to check the power of the Supreme Court that sentenced his father. Springing his dad was going to be one of President Flávio’s first acts, he maintained throughout the campaign. Whatever protection he may now hope to secure for himself in the U.S., there is no reason to imagine he will be able to do much for Jair. Any leverage he may have had rested on his ability to mobilize a sizable, disgruntled part of the Brazilian electorate. He can’t do that remotely. Ironically, in fact, Flávio’s flight may do more to discredit his father than anything Lula’s government could have done on its own. Jair’s political strength has always rested on the conviction among his supporters that he is an aggrieved fighter, a man willing to take on Brazil’s institutions and pay the price for doing so. His brash adult sons have now offered a different model of leadership: denouncing political persecution and vowing to fight on, even while plotting an escape to live lavishly abroad on funds likely secured through the biggest financial scandal in Brazilian history. It is difficult to imagine a more damaging repudiation of the family’s political brand for many rank-and-file bolsonaristas than the actions of Eduardo and Flávio. For years, the Bolsonaros have presented themselves as indispensable to Brazil’s conservative movement. There is some truth to this: Jair Bolsonaro was the only candidate since 1998 to win the presidency by vocally eschewing the left. The family’s appeal rested in part on the claim that only they possessed the courage to confront the country’s powerful institutions. Flávio’s flight has exposed the weakness in that claim. A movement that depends on the flighty failsons of an incarcerated one-term president and the goodwill of a soon-to-be lame duck in Washington is not much of a movement at all. It is a political inheritance in search of a custodian. And that is something that Trump, for all his talk of hemispheric dominance, cannot provide. He can issue visas, apply diplomatic pressure, and offer the Bolsonaros a platform from which to denounce Brazil’s government, but he cannot make a credible leader out of a whimpering coward.

articles.title: Daylight saving time is spooky this year: What to know about the 2026 clock change
articles.description: It’s that time of year again—when the sun sets earlier, the days get shorter, and the nights get colder as we say goodbye to daylight saving time (DST). DST ends this weekend, in the early morning hours after Halloween for most of the U.S. If you are one of the many people who find the time change confusing, remember the clock “falls back” and a majority of the U.S. “gains” one more hour of sleep each autumn. Here’s what else to know. When exactly does daylight saving time end in 2026? This Sunday, November 1, at 2 a.m. local time, we’ll turn back the clocks to 1 a.m., saying goodbye to daylight saving time until March 14, 2027. So we’ll get an extra hour of sleep? Yes—but although getting an extra hour of shut-eye sounds good, according to a growing consensus of health care providers, it actually may do more harm than good. While the majority of Americans (56%) favor making daylight saving permanent, a growing chorus of scientists and doctors disagree—including those from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and Stanford Medicine. These health care professionals argue that sticking to permanent standard time is healthier because it doesn’t disrupt the body’s natural circadian rhythm, which can lead to all sorts of health problems, including higher rates of stroke and obesity. Will daylight saving time permanently end in 2027? President Donald Trump has made it clear he wants to eliminate the current iteration of daylight saving time. But despite the U.S. House of Representatives passing the Sunshine Protection Act, it’s unclear when—or if—the Senate will give its stamp of approval, which is necessary to make it into law.
